interface.title: PrimerCheck Lite
interface.field: Molecular biology: PCR / qRT-PCR primer design
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment planning: in-silico screening of primers before ordering them and testing at the bench
interface.what_it_is_for: Screening a forward/reverse PCR primer pair against editable limits for length, GC%, Primer3 Tm, hairpin/dimer Tm, homopolymer runs, Tm difference and 3' GC count, under chosen reaction conditions, with an optional exact-amplicon check on a pasted template and JSON/HTML reports to keep with lab records.

data.note: I could not open the test files from the browser, and the app has no upload widget. I typed in the example primers shown as the field placeholders (F: ATGACCTACTTCGACGACGA, R: TCAGGATCTTGTCGATGTCG). The repository's examples/synthetic_template.fasta (and template.fasta) were NOT used. Every template-check result in this tree, including the coordinates 15–125 and the 110 bp length, comes from a 140-nt FASTA I wrote myself (>synthetic_target), which holds the forward site and the reverse-complement of the reverse primer. To test other states I also typed a deliberately weak reverse primer (TCAGGATCTTGTCGATAAAAAAA), an invalid one (TCAGGATCTXZTGTCG12) and a lower-case FASTA version of the reverse primer with spaces.

tree.general: Screen a pair of short DNA oligos before ordering them, under your own reaction conditions and acceptance limits, as a first check rather than a final approval, and keep a record of the result
tree.specific: Screen a forward/reverse PCR primer pair against lab-specific thresholds and assay conditions, check for an exact amplicon on a template, export JSON/HTML reports, and note that specificity still needs Primer-BLAST or in-silico PCR

features.name: Per-metric acceptance-range editor with optional limits
features.general: For each measured property, turn a lower and an upper limit on or off and set their values. Later checks and exports use exactly those limits, and an unset limit is stored as null
features.specific: In '3. Set acceptable ranges for every screening metric', each metric card (Length, Gc Percent, Tm C, Hairpin/Homodimer/Heterodimer Tm C, Homopolymer, Tm Difference C, Three Prime Gc Count) has 'Set minimum'/'Set maximum' checkboxes that show or hide number fields. The limits drive Status and warnings and are exported as primerchecklite-thresholds.json
steps: Tick or untick 'Set minimum' / 'Set maximum' on a metric card to show or hide its limit field
Type the limit value
Press 'Analyze primer pair' to apply the limits
Download the threshold settings to keep the criteria (disabled limits are stored as null)
serves_tasks: Adjust the acceptance limits to match your own protocol
Export the results and the criteria used

features.name: Reaction-condition panel feeding thermodynamic estimates
features.general: Set the physical and chemical conditions in a side panel, re-run, and see the derived quantities and pass/fail statuses change
features.specific: Sidebar 'Assay conditions' (monovalent salt mM, Mg/divalent salt mM, dNTP mM, primer nM), used by the Primer3 Tm, hairpin and dimer estimates. The values are written into the JSON report under 'settings'
steps: Type or step a concentration value in the sidebar
Press 'Analyze primer pair' (results do not update until you do)
Compare the Tm cards and statuses with the previous run
Confirm the conditions recorded in the exported JSON
serves_tasks: Enter the reaction chemistry that the calculations depend on
Compute all metrics for the pair

features.name: Out-of-range review list with a clean state
features.general: After a run, list each value that breaks a configured limit with its value and the range it broke, or show an all-clear message when nothing does, and explain why each property matters
features.specific: 'What needs review' tab: a red banner plus bullets such as 'Reverse primer: homopolymer is 7, outside the configured range (None to 4.0 bases)', a green 'No configured threshold warnings' banner when there are none, and the 'Why these parameters matter' expander
steps: Run the analysis
Open 'What needs review' and read each bullet
Change limits or the sequence and re-run to see warnings clear
Expand 'Why these parameters matter' to see what each metric means
serves_tasks: Review the list of values that fall outside the limits
Compare a second candidate against the same limits

features.name: Per-item metric table with status column
features.general: Show every computed property of each item as a Parameter/Value/Unit/Status table, so values that need review stand out
features.specific: 'Primer details' tab: one table per primer (Length … Three Prime Gc Count) with 'Within range'/'Review' status
steps: Open the 'Primer details' tab
Read each primer's values
Look for 'Review' in the Status column
Cross-check flagged rows against 'What needs review'
serves_tasks: Inspect each measured value and its pass/review status

features.name: Exact amplicon check on a pasted reference
features.general: Paste an optional reference sequence, re-run, and get a structured verdict on whether the pair gives exactly one product, with its coordinates and length
features.specific: Paste FASTA in 'Optional: add your target template'. The 'Template check' tab shows an info note when no template was given. Otherwise it shows JSON with status unique_exact_product (start_0_based, end_0_based_exclusive, length_bp), or no_unique_exact_product with a message. The result is also embedded in the JSON/HTML reports
steps: Expand the optional template section and paste a sequence or FASTA
Press 'Analyze primer pair'
Open 'Template check' and read the status, coordinates and length
Keep the verdict through the downloaded report
serves_tasks: Supply a reference sequence for a match check
See whether the pair yields a single product on the reference

features.name: Sequence paste field with cleanup and validation
features.general: Accept pasted sequences in common formats (header lines, mixed case, spaces), normalise them, and reject illegal characters with a message naming them
features.specific: Forward/Reverse primer text areas ignore FASTA headers, spaces and case. Invalid input shows 'Could not analyze these inputs: Only A, C, G, and T are supported. Invalid characters: 1, 2, X, Z'
steps: Paste a sequence, optionally as FASTA, in lower case or with spaces
Press Ctrl+Enter or Analyze to commit
Read the error banner if characters are invalid, then correct and re-run
serves_tasks: Make sure the sequences are read as intended: common pasted formats are accepted and illegal characters are rejected

features.name: Report export bundle
features.general: Download a machine-readable result, a human-readable report and a separate file of the criteria, so the evaluation can be kept with experiment records and repeated later
features.specific: 'Download reports' tab with three buttons. Download JSON gives sequences, metrics, statuses, warnings, settings, thresholds, amplicon and limitations. Download HTML report gives styled tables with review values in red, items to review, amplicon and limitations. Download threshold settings gives the thresholds JSON
steps: Run the analysis
Open 'Download reports'
Download the JSON, HTML and threshold files
Re-download after changing settings to capture the new state
serves_tasks: Export the results and the criteria used

features.name: Limitations panel pointing to an outside specificity check
features.general: A caveats panel shown with every result. It states what the screen cannot judge and names the genome-wide check to run before ordering
features.specific: 'Read before using the results' expander below all result tabs (not inside 'What needs review'). It lists limitations and refers users to NCBI Primer-BLAST or in-silico PCR
steps: Run the analysis
Expand 'Read before using the results' below the result tabs
Read the listed limitations
Plan the genome-wide specificity check it points to before ordering
serves_tasks: Read the stated limitations and note that a genome-wide specificity check is still needed before ordering

features.general: Summary tiles give each item's key derived value, the difference between the pair and the count of limit breaches, refreshed on each run so candidates can be compared at a glance
features.specific: Metric cards above the result tabs: Forward Tm, Reverse Tm, Tm difference (°C) and Warnings

Read the Forward/Reverse Tm and Tm difference cards
Read the Warnings count
Change a sequence, condition or limit, re-run and compare the cards

screens_never_reached: Primer details for the pair: heterodimer Tm and Tm difference appear only in the reports' 'pair' section and the Tm difference card. I saw no pair table in the Primer details tab.
Template check status for multiple products: I saw only unique_exact_product and no_unique_exact_product. I did not build a template that would give several products.
The rendered HTML report: I read its source but could not open it in the browser.
not_done: Using the repository's own example files (forward_primer.txt, reverse_primer.txt, template.fasta, examples/synthetic_template.fasta): the app has no upload widget and I cannot read test files directly. I used the placeholder primers and a template I built myself.
Downloading the per-primer table as CSV: the table's 'Download as CSV' button did not produce a file in this browser, even on a second try.
Collapsing the sidebar: the 'Collapse sidebar' button click timed out. I did not retry.
Changing the dNTP concentration: I left it at 0.20 mM. The other three conditions were changed.
Reading the 'Help for Minimum value' tooltip text on threshold fields: hovering showed no tooltip text.
The Streamlit main menu (theme, Rerun, Print, Record screen) is generic framework chrome. I opened it but did not use it as part of the task.

Generic table and JSON-viewer controls (table search for 'Tm', hiding the Unit column, collapsing the amplicon JSON, copying it to the clipboard, and pressing + twice to find the 0.01 step size) were used but are framework controls, not scientific steps, so they were removed from the tree.
